THIS APPEAL ALONG WITH M.F.A CROB, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.
The insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal being aggrieved by the award of compensation of Rs.16,46,000/- by the Tribunal for the death of Raju @ Raja.

2. It was the case of the claimants that while Raju was riding his TVS XL moped, it was hit by a Hero-Honda Splendor plus motorcycle, which resulted in serious injuries to him, to which he ultimately succumbed.
3. The insurer is challenging the order of the Tribunal principally on the ground that there is a serious discrepancy in relation to the manner in which the NC: 2024:KHC:51093 accident took place.

It is contended that the medical records at NIMHANS indicate that the version given to the hospital authorities was that the deceased was brought to the hospital with an alleged history of a road traffic accident when his two-wheeler was hit by a three-wheeler, and it is therefore contended that since the claim averments are to the contrary, i.e., as an accident between a two-wheeler and another two-wheeler, the entire accident is doubtful.
4. At the outset, it is to be stated here that the owner of the Hero-Honda motorcycle, which was stated to be the cause for the accident, chose to remain unrepresented despite service of notice.
In essence, therefore, the owner had admitted the assertions made in the claim petition i.e., his motorcycle was involved in the accident.
5. Furthermore, the Police after the investigation had laid a charge-sheet against the rider of the motor- cycle.

Apart from these two facts, it is also to be noticed here that the motor vehicle inspection report also indicates that there were damages to both the TVS XL moped, which is being driven by the deceased as well as to the motorcycle which was alleged to be the cause of the accident.

7. In my view, having regard to the fact that the attendant circumstances do indicate that there is an accident to the Hero-Honda motorcycle and to the TVS XL moped, and in the absence of a specific denial by the owner of the motorcycle, it would have to be held that the accident did occur between two 2- wheelers viz., TVS XL moped and Hero Honda motor- cycle, and the Tribunal was therefore Legal Manager vs Smt Munirathna on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109243957/
5 justified in coming to the same conclusion.
Consequently, in my view, there is no merit in the argument of the insurer that the vehicle was implicated.
8. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has arrived at the conclusion that the deceased was NC: 2024:KHC:51093 aged 34 years on the basis of the election ID card.
The claimants had also produced the Aadhar card which indicated that the deceased was born in 1979 and as the accident occurred in 2017, it is obvious that he was aged 36 years.
Therefore, it would be appropriate to take the age of the deceased as 36 years.
9. As far as the income is concerned, the Tribunal has taken the notional income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month as there was no proof of actual income.
In such cases, the sum of Rs.11,000/- determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accidents of the year 2017 will have to be adopted.

10. As per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi1, as the deceased was aged about 36 years, 40% of the same (Rs.4,400/-) is required to be National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others - (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC:51093 added to the said income as future prospects and the resultant income would be Rs.15,400/-.
11.

Since the deceased was survived by his wife, three children and parents, out of the said sum,
1/4th of the same (Rs.3,850/-) would have to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
The net income will be Rs.11,550/-.
12. As the deceased was aged 36 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma2, a multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.
13. Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.20,79,000/- (Rs.11,550/- x 12 x '15') towards "loss of dependency".

14. The claim petition was filed by Munirathna who claimed to be the first wife along with her two sons and they were also joined by Manjula, who was Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, (2009) 6 SCC 121 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:51093 stated to be the second wife along with her minor son, apart from the parents of the deceased.

i.e., in all a sum of Rs.2,42,000/- towards loss of love and affection.
16. The claimants would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/- under the "conventional heads".

21. Out of the balance, the share of second wife in a sum of Rs.24,200/- shall be released in her favour on proper identification.
22. The remaining sum shall be distributed equally among the first wife Munirathna and the parents of the deceased in equal proportion.

23. The amounts apportioned to the three children of the deceased shall be invested in a fixed deposit in their respective names in any nationalized bank or a post office deposit for a period of 10 years and their mothers are entitled to withdraw the accrued interest periodically.
24. The sums apportioned to the first wife Munirathna and the parents of the deceased shall be released in their favour in equal proportion after proper identification.
